query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and is intended to retain a favorable strength–ductility balance in its solidified solid-solution state, but its dynamic behavior across different temperatures and strain rates lacks a theoretical explanation. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could account for this behavior, and what controlled comparison within that regime would distinguish it? Specify predictions relative to a baseline, applicable boundaries, supporting evidence, and a falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Eliminating Co from the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy alters dislocation dynamics by reducing solute drag and dynamic strain aging effects, thereby shifting the onset of serration behavior and yield strengthening to lower temperatures and strain rates in the Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, homogeneous single-phase Co‐free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Conduct isothermal tensile tests with controlled strain rate jumps over a wide temperature range (from cryogenic ~77 K to elevated ~500 °C) and strain rate spectrum (10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ to 10² s⁻¹).
generation.conditions: Testing performed under precisely controlled temperatures and strain rates to capture transitions in dynamic behavior, with identical conditions applied to both the Co‐free alloy and the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline.
generation.structural_mediator: Variations in dislocation density and interactions (i.e., reduced solute-dislocation locking due to the absence of Co) mediate the dynamic response.
generation.mechanism: Removal of Co diminishes solute pinning (Cottrell atmospheres), lowering activation barriers for dislocation motion and shifting the regime of dynamic strain aging. This leads to an earlier onset of dislocation-driven strengthening and enhanced serration features in the stress-strain curves compared to the equiatomic alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic baseline, the Co‐free alloy will exhibit a pronounced increase in yield stress and marked serration behavior at lower temperatures or strain rates, with a steeper flow stress response when dynamic strain aging becomes operative.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy tested under identical dynamic mechanical conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to as-cast single-phase HEAs under the specified temperature (77 K to 500 °C) and strain rate (10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ to 10² s⁻¹) conditions and may not extend to alloys with additional processing or different phase structures.
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical temperature and strain rate thresholds for the onset of the altered dislocation dynamics remain uncertain, due to the complex interplay of thermal activation and solute effects. Quantitative differences may vary with subtle compositional or microstructural variances.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel isothermal tensile tests with strain rate jump protocols on both the Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy and the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline over a temperature range of 77 K to 500 °C and strain rates from 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ to 10² s⁻¹. Measure stress–strain curves with special attention to the onset and amplitude of serration behavior and yield stress evolution.
measurements: Yield stress vs. strain rate curves
Serration amplitude and frequency from stress–strain data
Post-deformation dislocation density via TEM analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Co‐free alloy does not show a significantly earlier onset of serration behavior or a steeper increase in yield stress with strain rate compared to the equiatomic baseline under identical conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Additionally, XRD, SEM, and TEM were used to thoroughly characterize the samples both before and after testing. The results are summarized below: Over a wide temperature range of RT-1223 K, the studied alloy exhibited excellent tensile mechanical properties. From RT to 678 K, the strength of the alloy was maintained above 1000 MPa; At 878–1078 K, the strength variation was small and no less than 800 MPa, and it nearly exceeded most commercial alloys. Coupled with an excellent cold workability, the alloy has the potential to be used as a new generation of high-temperature materials for the preparation of high-temperature-resistant parts in aerospace. That is, a work hardening occurred after yielding, and then a gradual softening until fracture. cited_evidence.kind: web:4.2. Mechanism for the Serration Behavior
cited_evidence.text: High-entropy alloys present serrations on the flow stress curves during the plastic deformation, often at a normal strain rate around 1 × 10−4 s−1 or at low temperatures. Serration behavior exhibits in the stress-strain curves of the Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloy at 7 K, 7.5 K, and 9 K at a strain rate of 4 × 10−4 s−1 []. The Al5Cr12Fe35Mn28Ni20 high-entropy alloy exhibits typical serration behaviors at the elevated temperatures of 573 K and 673 K, with a strain rate of 1 × 10−4 s−1 []. Several microstructure mechanisms are proposed to explain the serration behavior, e.g., the Portevin-Le Chatelier (PLC) effect. Serration behavior was supposed to be associated with Cottrell atmosphere interaction with moving dislocations, slip bands, and dynamic strain aging. chosen.why: This move directly addresses the unexplained dynamic behavior by testing the mechanistic hypothesis that the Co removal shifts the operative dislocation dynamics – for example, by reducing the contribution of a thermally activated dislocation mobility mechanism or altering dynamic strain aging. By systematically varying temperature and strain rate, the experiment distinguishes the conditions under which the Co‐free alloy exhibits an anomalous strength–ductility balance relative to the baseline, thereby providing testable predictions (e.g., an exponential increase in yield stress above a critical strain rate/temperature) and clear falsification criteria.
